mainTopic: Calendar uncertainty: testimony about קידוש החודש, רבי יוחנן's two-day גזירה for פסח, the doubt over יום כיפור in בבל, the spring rule for leap years, and a moon sign for sailors.
overview: This amud opens by closing an earlier question: we do not worry that two months in a row were declared short, because that would be widely known. Next, לוי arrives in בבל and points out that they are eating on the day that is יום כיפור in ארץ ישראל, yet he refuses to testify because he did not personally hear the בית דין declare 'מקודש'. רבי יוחנן then rules that wherever the ניסן messengers arrive but the תשרי messengers do not, people must keep two days of פסח, as a גזירה because of תשרי. He rebukes two of his students who saw such a town keeping one day and said nothing. Two stories follow about the doubt over יום כיפור: רבא used to fast two days, and רב נחמן was pained to hear, right after his fast, that the real day was tomorrow. רב הונא בר אבין tells רבא to add a leap month when winter would last until the 16th of ניסן, based on 'שמור את חודש האביב'. Finally, רב נחמן gives sailors a sign for burning חמץ: when the moon lasts all night until daybreak. The גמרא explains that at sea, with an open horizon, this already happens on the 14th.

steps.title: Two short months in a row would be widely known
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers an earlier worry: two consecutive months declared חסר would become public knowledge, so we do not need to worry that it happened without anyone hearing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If two months in a row are made short, people hear about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier discussion. Someone had asked whether we should worry that two months in a row were declared short (חסר), which would throw off the count of the days. The answer: something that unusual makes noise, so people would know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the months alternate between 29 and 30 days. Two 29-day months in a row is unusual, and unusual things get talked about. So we can rely on the regular pattern unless we have heard otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: months
short (29-day) months, called חָסֵר
it makes a sound, meaning it becomes public knowledge

phrases.english: Two months that are short (in a row)
phrases.notes: Each such month has 29 days instead of 30.

phrases.english: have a 'voice' (they become publicized).
phrases.notes: An unusual event gets talked about.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרֵי יַרְחֵי חַסִּירֵי קָלָא אִית לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question earlier about worrying over two consecutive חסר months.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reality: unusual calendar events become publicized.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have to worry that two months in a row were made חסר without our knowing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Such an event would be publicized, so we rely on the normal pattern.

steps.title: לוי notices Babylonians eating on יום כיפור of ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: לוי arrives in בבל on what they count as the 11th of תשרי. He remarks that they are eating on the day that is יום כיפור in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי came to בבל on the 11th of תשרי. He said: 'How tasty is the Babylonians' food on the great day (יום כיפור) of the West (ארץ ישראל)!'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a story. לוי points out that the Babylonians' calendar is one day off. Because אלול was made full (30 days) in ארץ ישראל, their 11th of תשרי is really the 10th, which is יום כיפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Babylonians had assumed אלול was short, as usual, so they were already done with יום כיפור. לוי knew that in ארץ ישראל אלול had been made 30 days. His sharp comment shows that the Babylonians were eating on the true יום כיפור.

keyTerms.meaning: happened to arrive
tasty is the dish
the great day, meaning יוֹם כִּפּוּר
'the West', meaning אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל

steps.confusionAlert: לוי is not praising the food. He is pointing out, with irony, that they are eating on what is really יום כיפור.

phrases.english: Levi arrived in Babylonia
on the eleventh of Tishrei (by their count).
phrases.notes: In ארץ ישראל it was only the 10th.

phrases.english: He said: How tasty is the dish of the Babylonians
on the great day (יום כיפור) of the West (Eretz Yisrael).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new story showing a real case where the calendar in בבל was off from ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this case the Babylonian count was a day ahead because אלול had been made full in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: לוי refuses to testify without hearing the בית דין himself
steps.stepSummary: The Babylonians ask Levi to testify so that they can keep יום כיפור now. He refuses, because he did not personally hear the בית דין declare 'מקודש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: 'Testify!' He said to them: 'I did not hear from the mouth of the court the word "מקודש" (sanctified).'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The people want לוי to give formal עדות so they can fix their calendar. לוי says he cannot, because his knowledge is not firsthand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing something is different from being able to testify to it. Testimony that would change the community's calendar needs someone who heard the בית דין's declaration of קידוש החודש directly. לוי knew the fact but lacked firsthand hearing, so he would not give עדות.

keyTerms.meaning: testify!
the court (here, the court that sanctifies the month)
'sanctified', the בית דין's declaration that the new month has begun

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that changing the calendar depends on proper עדות about the בית דין's declaration, not on general knowledge or rumor.

phrases.english: They said to him: Testify!
He said to them: I did not hear
from the mouth of the court "It is sanctified."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the לוי story with the people's request and his refusal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may testify about קידוש החודש only if he heard the בית דין's declaration 'מקודש' himself.
steps.whatToRemember: לוי knew the right date but would not testify, because valid עדות requires hearing the בית דין's 'מקודש' firsthand.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's ruling: two days of פסח where תשרי messengers don't reach
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן announces that places reached by the ניסן messengers but not by the תשרי messengers must keep two days of פסח. This is a גזירה because of תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן used to announce: Any place that the messengers of ניסן reach, but the messengers of תשרי do not reach, should keep two days. This is a decree in ניסן because of תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching. רבי יוחנן sets a rule for places that, by ניסן, know the correct date of פסח but, in תשרי, would not know the correct date of סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The messengers do not travel on ראש השנה or יום כיפור, so in תשרי they reach less far than in ניסן. A place reached in ניסן could keep one day of פסח with certainty. But if it did, people would come to keep one day of סוכות too, when they really are in doubt. So the חכמים decreed two days even in ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: publicly announces
messengers (sent to report when the month began)
let them keep two days (of יום טוב)
a rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
because of, on account of

steps.confusionAlert: In ניסן these places actually know the right date. The second day is not because of doubt about פסח. It is only a safeguard so that they will not keep one day in תשרי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is an important source for how יום טוב שני was set up for places outside ארץ ישראל: it can apply even where the doubt exists only in תשרי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan used to announce:
Any place that the messengers of Nisan reach,
but the messengers of Tishrei do not reach —
phrases.notes: Tishrei messengers lose travel days because of ראש השנה and יום כיפור.

phrases.english: let them observe two days.
It is a decree in Nisan because of Tishrei.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַכְרִיז רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּמָטוּ שְׁלוּחֵי נִיסָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the לוי story to a formal ruling about places on the edge of the messengers' reach.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Places reached by ניסן messengers but not תשרי messengers keep two days of פסח, as a גזירה because of תשרי.

steps.title: Two students see a town keeping one day and stay silent
steps.stepSummary: רבי אייבו בר נגרי and רבי חייא בר אבא visit a town covered by רבי יוחנן's ruling. The town keeps only one day, and the students say nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אייבו בר נגרי and רבי חייא בר אבא came to a certain place that the ניסן messengers reached but the תשרי messengers did not. The people kept one day, and the rabbis said nothing at all to them.
steps.whatsHappening: A story about רבי יוחנן's ruling in practice. The students see people keeping only one day of פסח in exactly the kind of place his ruling covers, and they do not correct them. This sets up רבי יוחנן's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The town kept one day because in ניסן they knew the date with certainty, but that is exactly what רבי יוחנן's גזירה forbids. The students' silence is the problem that the next step addresses.

keyTerms.meaning: place, locale
one day
and nothing at all

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַיְיבוּ בַּר נַגָּרֵי וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Aivu bar Naggarei and Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba
happened to come to a certain place
that the messengers of Nisan would reach
but the messengers of Tishrei would not reach,
and they (the locals) kept one day,
and they (the rabbis) said nothing at all to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַיְיבוּ בַּר נַגָּרֵי וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אִיקְּלַעוּ לְהָהוּא אַתְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a real case where רבי יוחנן's ruling from step 4 was not followed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A town covered by the גזירה kept one day, and the visiting students did not object.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is upset and repeats his ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן hears what happened, becomes angry, and reminds his students of his ruling: two days, as a גזירה in ניסן because of תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן heard and was upset. He said to them: 'Didn't I tell you that wherever the ניסן messengers reach but the תשרי messengers don't, they should keep two days, as a decree in ניסן because of תשרי?!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן rebukes his students for staying silent. He repeats his ruling word for word to stress that it is binding and should have been enforced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא repeats the exact wording of step 4, but now for a new purpose: a rebuke. That repetition shows the ruling was binding and that the students should have corrected the town.

keyTerms.meaning: became angry, was upset
didn't I tell you?

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's גזירה is binding: places reached by the ניסן messengers but not the תשרי messengers must keep two days of פסח, and תלמידים are expected to make sure it is kept.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan heard and became angry.
He said to them: Did I not tell you
wherever the messengers of Nisan reach
but the messengers of Tishrei do not reach
they should observe two days,
a decree in Nisan because of Tishrei!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוחנן reacts to the students' silence from step 5 by repeating his ruling from step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The גזירה of keeping two days in ניסן because of תשרי stands firm and must be enforced.

steps.title: רבא fasts two days of יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: רבא used to fast two days for יום כיפור because of the doubt about the date. Once, his second day turned out to be the real one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא used to fast for two days on יום כיפור. One time, it turned out that the real day matched his practice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. רבא fasted two days on יום כיפור because he was unsure which day was correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בבל, they normally counted אלול as 29 days. If the בית דין made אלול 30 days, יום כיפור would really fall on what בבל called the 11th of תשרי, just like in the לוי story. רבא covered both options by fasting both days, and one year his extra day really was the true יום כיפור.

keyTerms.meaning: A fast (here, the fast of יום כיפור)
Accustomed, used to doing something regularly
It turned out according to him (his practice proved correct)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא fasted two days because of a rule like the two days of יום טוב in חוץ לארץ. חז"ל did not require two days of יום כיפור, because fasting two days in a row is too hard. This was רבא's own personal strictness.

phrases.english: Rava was accustomed
to sit fasting for two days (on Yom Kippur).
phrases.notes: Out of concern that אלול had been made 30 days.

phrases.english: One time it turned out in accordance with him.
phrases.notes: That year אלול was 30 days, so his second day was the real יום כיפור.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא הֲוָה רְגִיל דַּהֲוָה יָתֵיב בְּתַעֲנִיתָא תְּרֵי יוֹמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the לוי story (Steps 2-3): in בבל, יום כיפור might really fall on what they call the 11th of תשרי. This shows one אמורא's personal response to that doubt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא personally fasted two days of יום כיפור because of the doubt, and once the second day really was יום כיפור.

steps.title: A man tells רב נחמן that tomorrow is יום כיפור in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן fasted a full day of יום כיפור. In the evening, a man came and told him that tomorrow is יום כיפור in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן fasted the whole day of יום כיפור. In the evening, a certain man came and said to him: Tomorrow is the Great Day in the West (ארץ ישראל).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second story. רב נחמן has just finished his fast, and he hears news that the real יום כיפור is actually tomorrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the exact case רבא was worried about: אלול was made 30 days, so בבל fasted one day too early. Now רב נחמן would have to fast again tomorrow, which means two days in a row. This sets up his reaction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: In the evening
The Great Day, a name for יום כיפור
The West, meaning ארץ ישראל (it lies west of בבל)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman sat fasting
the entire day of Yom Kippur.
In the evening, a certain man came,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לִמְחַר יוֹמָא רַבָּה בְּמַעְרְבָא.
phrases.english: and said to him: Tomorrow is the Great Day in the West.
phrases.notes: Meaning the real יום כיפור is tomorrow, so he must fast again.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן יְתֵיב בְּתַעֲנִיתָא כּוּלֵּיהּ יוֹמֵי דְּכִיפּוּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about the same doubt. רבא planned ahead for it, while רב נחמן only found out after finishing his fast.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Word arrived that יום כיפור in ארץ ישראל was the next day, so רב נחמן had to fast again.

steps.title: רב נחמן's pained reaction to the news
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks the man where he is from. He answers 'דמהריא'. רב נחמן plays on the name, saying 'Blood will be his end', and quotes the פסוק 'Our pursuers were swift'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן asked him: Where are you from? He said: From דמהריא. רב נחמן said: 'Blood will be his end.' And he applied the פסוק to him: 'Our pursuers were swift.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the רב נחמן story by showing how hard the news was for him. He makes a wordplay on the man's town and quotes a פסוק from איכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The town name דמהריא sounds like 'דם' (blood). רב נחמן uses this to say that a second fast day will be like having his blood spilled, since 'his end' is a polite way of referring to himself. The פסוק 'Our pursuers were swift' means the messenger came 'too fast': had he arrived a little later, they would already have eaten and drunk before the second fast began.

keyTerms.meaning: Where are you from?
Blood will be his end, a wordplay on the name דמהריא
Our pursuers were swift (איכה ד:יט)

steps.whatToRemember: Both stories show that in בבל the doubt about יום כיפור was real. Still, חז"ל never required two days of fasting. Only individuals like רבא took it on, and it was very hard, as רב נחמן's reaction shows.

phrases.english: He (Rav Nachman) said to him: Where are you from?
He said to him: From Damihareya.
He said to him: Blood will be his end.
phrases.notes: Wordplay on the town name. 'His end' politely refers to רב נחמן himself, who will suffer from fasting two days.

phrases.english: He read about him: 'Our pursuers were swift.'
phrases.notes: Had the messenger come a little later, they would already have eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly continues the story from Step 8 and gives רב נחמן's reaction to the news.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן expresses how painful a second fast day would be through a wordplay and a פסוק.

steps.title: רב הונא בר אבין's rule for adding a leap month
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר אבין sends a message to רבא: if the winter season would last until the 16th of ניסן, make the year a leap year, and do not worry about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר אבין sent to רבא: When you see that the season of טבת (winter) extends until the 16th of ניסן, add a month to that year, and do not worry about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic about the calendar: when to make a leap year. רב הונא בר אבין gives רבא a clear rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The year has four seasons (תקופות), and the winter season is called תקופת טבת. If calculations show that winter would still be going on through the 16th of ניסן (the middle of פסח), the year must get an extra אדר. 'Do not worry about it' means this reason alone is enough, and no other supporting reason is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The winter season, which starts around טבת
Make it a leap year by adding a month
Year
And do not worry about it (no further reason is needed)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the main reasons for a leap year: פסח must fall in the spring, so a month is added when the spring season would otherwise begin too late.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר אָבִין לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Avin sent to Rava:
When you see that the season of Tevet extends
until the sixteenth of Nisan,
phrases.notes: That is, the spring season would only begin after the 16th.

phrases.english: make that year a leap year
and do not worry about it,

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר אָבִין לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new calendar topic. It is linked to the previous material only by the general theme of fixing the calendar and by the name רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the winter season would extend to the 16th of ניסן, add a leap month that year without needing any other reason.

steps.title: The verse source: spring must fall in ניסן
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק 'Guard the month of spring'. It teaches that the spring season must begin within ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Guard the month of spring.' This means: guard the spring of the season, so that it falls in the month of ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: The message from רב הונא בר אבין continues by giving the source in the תורה for his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'שמור' (guard) is read as an instruction to make sure the spring season (אביב של תקופה) begins inside ניסן, early enough for פסח. If winter would last past the 16th, spring would not arrive in time. So you must 'guard' it by adding a month, which pushes ניסן later.

keyTerms.meaning: Guard the month of spring (דברים טז:א)
The spring of the season, meaning the start of the spring season

steps.whatToRemember: A leap year is required when spring would otherwise start after the 16th of ניסן, because the תורה requires פסח to be in the spring ('שמור את חודש האביב').

phrases.english: as it is written: 'Guard the month of spring,'
guard the spring of the season
so that it falls in the month of Nisan.
phrases.notes: That is, in the early (new) part of ניסן, before פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק that supports the rule in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a year must be made a leap year if the winter season would extend to the 16th of ניסן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים טז:א, 'שמור את חודש האביב', read as 'guard the spring season so that it falls in ניסן'.

steps.title: רב נחמן's moon sign for sailors
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן tells sailors who cannot know when the month began to burn their חמץ when they see the moon last all night until daybreak.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to sailors: You won't know when the month was set. So when you see the moon lasting until daybreak, burn your חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives sailors, who are cut off from news of בית דין's calendar, a practical sign in the sky for knowing when to burn חמץ before פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sailors leaving before ניסן won't hear which day בית דין declared ראש חודש. So רב נחמן gives them a natural clue instead. When the moon is full, it rises at sunset and stays up all night until sunrise, and that tells them they are in the middle of ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: Sailors, literally 'those who go down to the sea'
The fixing of the month, meaning which day בית דין declared ראש חודש
The moon
Lasts until the day, meaning it shines all night until daybreak
Burn the חמץ (leaven)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to them
to those sailors:
You, who do not know
the fixing of the month,
when you see the moon
that lasts until daybreak,
phrases.notes: It shines the whole night, from sunset until sunrise.

phrases.english: burn the leaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב נַחְמָן לְהָנְהוּ נָחוֹתֵי יַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of people who are unsure of the calendar date, this time applied to sailors and פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sailors should burn חמץ when they see the moon lasting the whole night until daybreak.

steps.title: The full-night moon comes on the 15th, but we burn on the 14th
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the moon lasts all night, answers that it is the 15th, and then challenges רב נחמן: we burn חמץ on the 14th!
steps.simpleTranslation: When does the moon last until daybreak? On the 15th. But we burn חמץ from the 14th!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first asks a quick setup question about which night the moon lasts until morning. It then uses the answer to challenge רב נחמן's sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the moon only lasts all night on the 15th, then a sailor following רב נחמן's sign would burn his חמץ a day late, on פסח itself. The halacha requires burning on the 14th, ערב פסח. So the sign seems to give the wrong day.

keyTerms.meaning: When?
Fifteen (the 15th of the month)
Fourteen (the 14th of the month, ערב פסח)
But surely, a word that opens a challenge

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'אימת משלים — בחמיסר' is not the challenge itself. It is a short setup that lays down a fact. The real attack comes with 'והא'.

phrases.english: When does it last until daybreak?
On the fifteenth.
But we burn from the fourteenth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the sign given by רב נחמן in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's sign of the moon lasting until daybreak
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The moon lasts all night only on the 15th, so the sign would make sailors burn חמץ a day too late, after the deadline of the 14th.

steps.title: At sea, the moon already lasts all night on the 14th
steps.stepSummary: For sailors, who see the whole open horizon, the moon already appears to last until daybreak on the 14th.
steps.simpleTranslation: For them, to whom the world is open, the moon lasts until daybreak already from the 14th.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Out at sea the view is different, so the sign does point to the 14th.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On land, mountains and buildings block the horizon, so on the 14th the moon seems to set before sunrise. At sea nothing blocks the view, so the moon is visible all the way until daybreak already on the 14th. This means רב נחמן's sign works for sailors, and only for them.

keyTerms.meaning: For them (the sailors)
The world is revealed to them, meaning they have an open, unblocked horizon

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's moon sign is for sailors only. Because they have an open horizon, the moon appears to last all night already on the 14th, which is the right day to burn חמץ.

phrases.english: For them, to whom the world is revealed,
phrases.notes: At sea the horizon is wide open, with nothing blocking the view.

phrases.english: it lasts until daybreak from the fourteenth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 13 by limiting the sign to the special viewing conditions at sea.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the sign is defined by sailors' viewing conditions, not by what people see on land.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The moon lasts all night only on the 15th, so the sign gives the wrong day.
steps.terutzMaskana: At sea the open horizon makes the moon visible until daybreak already on the 14th, so the sign is correct for sailors.
